newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares dip but U.S.-inspired rally foreseen.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares dip but U.S.-inspired rally foreseen.

text.p: Danish share prices closed a little lower on Wednesday, with dealers foreseeing a positive day ahead after stocks and bonds got off to a good start on Wall Street with United States trends set to determine the way the market would go in Europe.
"America is going to set the trend tomorrow even if some people are still in the sidelines inhibited by talk of possible new government taxes on stock investments," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index closed 0.15 point down at 125.78 in overall bourse turnover of 864 million crowns. The KFX December future fell 0.10 point to 126.35 with 40 contracts traded.

Fourth biggest bank Jyske Bank unveiled first nine-months 1996 results showing solid advances but leaving expectations for whole year profits unchanged at between 650-750 million crowns before tax, securities and extraordinary items.

The Jyske Bank share closed four crowns higher at 421, while Unibank and Den Danske Bank, although rallying after the latest subdued U.S. key data bolstered bonds, finished the day three and two crowns down respectively at 267 and 415.
